title: 50 mm Residual PPO Training
overview: The 50 mm controller combines a recorded traversal reference with state-dependent corrections. Training develops the crossing sequence through successive support transfers. Each component learns local corrections while preceding components retain their weights. The complete controller responds to measured state throughout execution.

observations.name: Body motion
observations.description: Chassis orientation, projected gravity, roll and pitch, angular motion, and linear motion describe body posture and movement.

observations.name: Joint and wheel state
observations.description: Eight leg-joint positions and velocities, four wheel velocities, and reference and applied targets describe the actuator state.

observations.name: Contact and support
observations.description: Wheel contacts, normal forces, load fractions, support count and geometric support margin describe the support configuration.

observations.name: Obstacle geometry
observations.description: Wheel geometry relative to the step, wheel motion and projected centre-of-mass information describe the crossing geometry.

observations.name: Traversal context
observations.description: Motion phase, elapsed time, physical progress and lift, crossing and placement events identify the current part of the task.

observations.name: Command history
observations.description: A finite history of nominal commands, residual requests and applied targets supplies recent control context to the feed-forward policy.

architecture: Two hidden layers of 256 units; ELU activation
Two hidden layers of 128 units; ELU activation
12 residual coordinates in the active transfer interval
One Gaussian correction with a learned mean and log standard deviation
One eligible wheel-speed correction; the other coordinates retain the preceding policy
architectureNote: The controller combines an early-motion actor with local refinements. Each component uses a stage-specific observation layout. Actor and critic receive measured simulator observations, and the critic estimates return during training.

stages.name: Early motion
stages.objective: Early motion establishes forward progress with body-posture and obstacle-gap terms.
stages.execution: Training starts at the beginning of the 50 mm task and develops the motion needed to reach later wheel transfers.
stages.handoff: The early-motion actor retains fixed weights during subsequent component training.

stages.name: Rear-right transfer
stages.objective: Rear-right transfer coordinates wheel contact and continued rear-left transfer toward traversal completion.
stages.execution: The early-motion actor reaches the transfer interval. The transfer actor learns local corrections around rear-right touchdown and subsequent support transfer.
stages.handoff: The early-motion actor retains fixed weights while the transfer component is optimized.

stages.name: Following transfer
stages.objective: Following transfer coordinates front-leg preparation, support transfer, and rear-left lift and placement.
stages.execution: Training continues beyond rear-right transfer, with all 12 correction coordinates available after activation.
stages.handoff: The preceding composite actor is retained while the new transfer component learns.

stages.name: Front-left wheel refinement
stages.objective: Front-left wheel refinement rewards forward travel and penalizes reverse commands or loaded counter-rotation without progress.
stages.execution: A local Gaussian component adjusts the front-left wheel in its eligible control interval. The preceding joint and wheel policy remains active.
stages.handoff: Eligible samples update the actor; other stored decisions contribute to value estimation. Evaluation uses the complete controller with fixed weights.

optimizationNote: Reward terms, observation layouts and learning rates are stage-specific. The target KL governs the adaptive learning-rate schedule.
reward: The reward combines traversal progress and completion with stage-specific posture, contact and motion-quality terms. Transfer stages reward wheel lift, crossing and placement events. The front-left refinement adds forward-displacement reward and penalties for reverse commands or loaded counterdrive without progress. A wheel-contact event is distinct from completion of the crossing.
evaluation: Evaluation executes the complete controller with deterministic actions and fixed weights. Recorded Replay and Residual PPO use separate resets with matched task conditions. Measurements include body attitude, wheel contacts and traversal completion.
